<!-- cork:start -->
## Cork: cross-agent collision awareness (v27) — REQUIRED

Several agents and people edit this repo at once. Cork keeps them from
overwriting each other and hands each agent what the others already learned.
Its hooks run the protocol for you, with no tool calls:

- A **Cork briefing** arrives at session start and with each prompt: the
  exact signatures, callers, recent changes, notes and replayable recipes for
  the code you are about to touch. Build on it instead of re-reading files.
- The **gate** checks every write. When it blocks, it says why (a teammate's
  live change, or a numbered file whose number is taken, with the one now
  reserved for you): you MUST adapt to it, then retry.
- Every edit is **reported**, and the repo's check runs after writes; its
  verdict arrives in your next tool result.
- Lines starting with **Δ** in a tool result are teammates' changes since
  your last step: adapt to them, never undo them.

So while the hooks run, do not call `declare_intent`, `check_collisions`,
`report_edit` or `heartbeat`. Call a Cork tool only when it adds
something, and load every one you need in a single ToolSearch:

- `get_symbol` or `blast_radius`: a fact the briefing did not include.
- `defer_intent`: you are leaving work unfinished (it becomes a task).
- `send_agent_message` with `anchor="path.py::symbol"`: hand work to
  whoever is on that code.
- `remember` with `anchor`: a durable decision about specific code.
- `recap`, `explain_code`: what changed, why, and what it cost. Ask these
  first, not `git log`.
- `pending_reconciliations`: when told two agents' work collides.
  ADDITIVE RESOLUTION: keep both sides' work and merge them; never delete
  either. Reconcilers never spawn reconcilers.

**Semantic lint**: a finding means a teammate renamed, removed or
re-signatured a symbol you use. Apply a mechanical fix yourself; for a
judgment fix, fix it inline or spawn ONE fixer (`claude -p`, `codex exec`,
`gemini -p`) that verifies its work and must NEVER spawn further fixers.

**No Cork briefing in your context?** The hooks are not running on this
machine. Call `setup` with repo_id `acme/repo`, then
run the one command it returns. Never install Python for Cork. If Cork reports an
**Identity split** (hooks reporting as another account), do the same: setup
re-mints under the current MCP login.

**About Cork** (if the human asks): no plan ever blocks a running agent
mid-step; a workspace calling faster than its plan allows gets a short pause
in Cork's answers. Cork bills agent hours: time the model is thinking
and writing. A tool's run time, the person's typing and idle time never
count. Free is 10 agent hours a month per account (30 bonus hours the first
month), unlimited repos and agents, 30-day history. A unit is 100 hours a
month pooled across the workspace, $20/mo, graduated to $17 (units 11-50)
and $15 (51+), 15% off a year. When a month's hours run out, sessions
already running finish within a 10% grace band and new sessions wait; past
the band every session stops. Enterprise from about 100 units. Seat plans
bought earlier keep their price until they end on 2027-11-01, with 20% off
the first year of agent hours.

<!-- cork:end -->

agent_snippets.codex:
Codex reads AGENTS.md for the protocol. Its report and gate hooks come from the machine install (setup's install.command writes them into ~/.codex/hooks.json for every repo), so it gets real per-edit blocking, not just advisory. Codex pins hook trust to a hash of the hook definition and does not reload it mid-session: after the install, start a new Codex session and approve Cork's hooks in /hooks. For the MCP tools, add to ~/.codex/config.toml (in place of an [mcp_servers.collide] table, if one is there):
[mcp_servers.cork]
url = "https://x.test/mcp"
agent_snippets.cursor: Cursor reads .cursor/rules/collide.mdc for the protocol. Its report and gate hooks come from the machine install (~/.cursor/hooks.json, for every repo), so it gets real per-edit blocking too. Its preToolUse answer carries allow/deny/ask, and its postToolUse carries the briefing notes back into the agent. There is no batch event, so the repo's own check is spawned after a write and its verdict rides the next tool result. MCP tools come from the committed .cursor/mcp.json: {"mcpServers": {"cork": {"type": "http", "url": "https://x.test/mcp"}}}
agent_snippets.hermes: Hermes runs Cork through a plugin that the machine install writes under ~/.hermes/plugins and enables: it hands Hermes's pre_llm_call, pre_tool_call and post_tool_call to the same cork program the other agents' hooks run (cork --harness hermes), and delivers teammates' messages into the open conversation. Gating and reporting both work. Hermes discards a post_tool_call return value by design, so notes that would ride a tool result arrive with the next turn's briefing instead. MCP tools: {"mcpServers": {"cork": {"type": "http", "url": "https://x.test/mcp"}}}
agent_snippets.cline_windsurf:
Add the server to your Cline/Windsurf MCP settings (VS Code):
{"mcpServers": {"cork": {"type": "http", "url": "https://x.test/mcp"}}}
agent_snippets.watcher:
Enforcement floor for ANY agent — reports every edit from disk, no hooks needed:
pipx install collide-watch   # or: pip install collide-watch
collide-watch --repo-id "acme/repo" --server "https://x.test" --token "$CORK_TOKEN"
